subtitle: When a Sanskrit Line Heard the Yavanas March

panels.shot: split composition, half showing a solemn Pushyamitra on a Magadhan rampart, half showing Menander in Hellenistic armor over a map, with a palm-leaf manuscript looming between them
panels.action: Pushyamitra Shunga stands on a stone wall over the Ganga plain, cloak whipping in the wind, while opposite him Menander I leans over a rugged frontier map; between them, larger than both, floats an open palm-leaf manuscript etched with faint, unreadable lines.

dialogue.text: In an age when Yavana kings rode from the northwest and Magadha still dreamed it ruled all, a quiet grammar lesson caught the thunder between Pushyamitra Shunga and Menander of the frontier.

i18n.hi: जब यवन राजा उत्तर-पश्चिम से घोड़े दौड़ा रहे थे और मगध अभी भी सपने में सम्राट था, तब एक चुप सा व्याकरण पाठ पुष्यमित्र शुंग और सीमा के मेनान्दर के बीच गूंजती गरज को पकड़ बैठा।

panels.shot: wide aerial of the subcontinent, clouds casting shadows over Magadha, the northwest passes and the central Ganga plain
panels.action: A bird’s-eye view of the Indian subcontinent shows the rich Ganga plain around Pataliputra, the dusty northwest passes, and the central towns like Saketa and Madhyamika marked only by their landscape features.

dialogue.text: A few generations after Ashoka, the land between the Ganga and the Indus no longer answered to one emperor; old Magadha still sat in the east, but new horsemen watched from the northwest.

i18n.hi: अशोक के कुछ पीढ़ी बाद, गंग और सिन्धु के बीच की धरती किसी एक सम्राट को नहीं सुनती थी; पुराना मगध पूर्व में बैठा था, पर नए घुड़सवार उत्तर-पश्चिम से सब देख रहे थे।

panels.shot: medium shot of a crumbling Mauryan pillar beside a newer fortress wall
panels.action: A weathered stone pillar with faint Mauryan-style polish leans near a newer, rougher brick fort wall, overgrown grass creeping between them, under a hazy sky.

dialogue.text: The Mauryan lion pillars still glowed in the sun, but their power was memory; in their shadow, successor kings argued over tax, tribute and the right to command men to die.

i18n.hi: मौर्य के सिंह-स्तंभ अब भी धूप में चमकते थे, पर उनकी ताकत बस याद थी; उनकी छाया में उत्तराधिकारी राजा कर, नज़राना और मौत तक भेजने के हक़ पर भिड़ते थे।

panels.shot: two-panel style close, left on Pushyamitra in court, right on Menander in a frontier camp
panels.action: On the left, Pushyamitra Shunga sits in a modest Magadhan court, grey-bearded, a soldier-turned-king in plain ornaments; on the right, Menander I in Hellenistic cuirass and Indian scarf studies a frontier landscape, coins and scrolls on his table.

dialogue.text: In Pataliputra, the Shunga general Pushyamitra claimed Magadha’s throne; far away, an Indo-Greek king called Menander ruled from the northwest, his minting dies speaking of Yavana power and restless movement.

i18n.hi: पाटलिपुत्र में शुंग सेनापति पुष्यमित्र ने मगध की गद्दी थामी; दूर उत्तर-पश्चिम में यवन राजा मेनान्दर बैठा था, उसकी टकसाल की मुद्राएँ यवन ताकत और बेचैन सफ़र की बात करती थीं।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of Menander addressing his captains before a mobile camp near a river crossing
panels.action: Menander I stands before a mixed host of Greek-style and Indian soldiers in a frontier camp by a river, trees bending in the wind, his arm raised toward distant eastern hills.

dialogue.speaker: pushyamitra_shunga_and_menander_i
dialogue.text: The road east is not a dream; it is a test of how far a king’s name can travel.

i18n.hi: पूरब की राह कोई सपना नहीं; यह कसौटी है कि राजा का नाम कितनी दूर जा सकता है।

panels.shot: close-up of Indo-Greek coins on a trader’s palm, background blurred
panels.action: A trader’s rough hand holds gleaming silver Indo-Greek coins, one showing a diademed bust, another a Greek legend and Indian symbol, with blurred caravan tents behind.

dialogue.text: Coins in strange letters crossed caravans and rivers, stamped with Indo-Greek names; they tell us now that Yavana courts had become part of the political sky over northwestern India.

i18n.hi: अजनबी लिपि वाले सिक्के काफिलों और नदियों को पार करते, उन पर खुदे यवन-यूनानी नाम; वे बताते हैं कि यवन दरबार अब उत्तर-पश्चिम भारत के सियासी आसमान का हिस्सा बन चुके थे।

panels.shot: wide shot of Saketa’s city walls and gates, watched by anxious townsfolk
panels.action: A walled city with wooden gates and watchtowers rises from a dusty plain, locals in simple cloths look up from markets and wells toward the northwest road, anxiety on their faces.

dialogue.text: Between these powers lay Saketa in the central Ganga plain, a city of merchants and officials used to Magadhan orders, not to the thought of Yavana soldiers at its gate.

i18n.hi: इन दोनों ताकतों के बीच गंगा के मैदान में साकेत था, व्यापारी और अफ़सरों का शहर, जिसे आदत थी मगध के हुक्मों की, यवन फौजों की सोच की नहीं जो उसके फाटक पर हों।

panels.shot: interior of an ancient classroom, focus on Patanjali with students around
panels.action: Inside a simple hall with clay lamps, Patanjali sits cross-legged before young students, palm-leaf manuscripts beside him, his gaze calm but intent, while a faint rumble seems to vibrate the hanging oil lamp.

dialogue.text: And in another town, perhaps close in time, a scholar named Patanjali taught Sanskrit grammar; he listened for tiny sounds in verbs, yet the world outside pressed into his examples.

i18n.hi: और किसी दूसरे नगर में, शायद इसी दौर में, पाणिनि का शिष्य पतंजलि नाम का विद्वान संस्कृत व्याकरण पढ़ाता था; वह धातु के सूक्ष्म स्वर सुनता, पर बाहर की दुनिया उसके उदाहरणों में घुस आती।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of Patanjali’s hand writing on a palm leaf
panels.action: A hand grips a stylus over a palm leaf, incising neat Sanskrit characters, the letters crisp against the pale surface as a student leans in, eyes wide.

dialogue.text: To show how a verb could act in the past, he did not choose a harmless tale; he wrote of Yavanas who had surrounded Saketa and Madhyamika, as if the siege still echoed in his pupils’ ears.

i18n.hi: भूतकाल दिखाने के लिए उसने कोई मासूम कहानी नहीं चुनी; उसने यवनों के साकेत और मध्यामिक को घेर लेने की बात लिखी, जैसे घेरा अभी भी शिष्यों के कानों में गूंजता हो।

panels.shot: medium shot of students reacting, some tense, some whispering
panels.action: Several students, wrapped in simple shawls, look up from their leaves; one clutches his beads tighter, another glances toward the doorway as if half expecting an alarm.

dialogue.text: The Mahabhashya’s line is brief, almost dry, yet it assumes its audience knows: Yavana armies have stood before Indian walls; the grammar of their fear needs no gloss.

i18n.hi: महाभाष्य की वह पंक्ति छोटी है, लगभग सूखी, पर मान कर चलती है कि श्रोता जानते हैं: यवन सेनाएँ भारतीय दीवारों के सामने आ खड़ी हुई हैं; उनके डर का व्याकरण अलग से समझाने की ज़रूरत नहीं।

panels.shot: wide dramatic shot of Yavana forces outside Saketa, but viewed from behind the walls
panels.action: From atop Saketa’s wall, we see a distant host of foreign-looking soldiers and elephants arrayed in the plains, banners rippling, dust hanging in the air, but no clash shown, only tense stillness.

dialogue.text: We do not know if those Yavanas actually took Saketa, or if they turned away; we only know that their presence was vivid enough to serve as a plain, unornamented example of past action.

i18n.hi: हमें पता नहीं कि वे यवन सच में साकेत में घुसे या लौट गए; बस इतना जानते हैं कि उनकी मौजूदगी इतनी तेज़ थी कि सीधे, बिना सजावट के भूतकाल सिखाने का उदाहरण बन गई।

panels.shot: wide shot of Madhyamika’s hill fort with distant approaching columns
panels.action: A hill-fort town like Madhyamika clings to rocky heights, fields below dotted with tiny figures in organized lines, moving slowly along a road toward the city.

dialogue.text: Madhyamika too appears in that same breath of grammar; the Yavanas have been there, says the line, and scholars argue still whether this means a raid, a siege, or the mere terror of rumour.

i18n.hi: मध्यामिक का नाम भी उसी सांस में आता है; पंक्ति कहती है, यवन वहाँ तक जा चुके हैं, और विद्वान आज भी लड़ते हैं कि यह हल्का धावा था, घेरेबंदी, या केवल अफ़वाह का साया।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a palm leaf of the Mahabhashya placed beside a worn sword
panels.action: A palm leaf manuscript lies on a woven mat beside a sheathed, nicked sword; sunlight from a window falls across both, dust motes floating in the beam.

dialogue.text: The Mahabhashya is a grammar, not a war chronicle; it names no commanders, counts no dead, yet its simple mention proves that frontier shock had entered the very teaching of language.

i18n.hi: महाभाष्य तो व्याकरण है, युद्ध-वृत्तांत नहीं; न सेनापति गिनता, न लाशें, पर उसका साधारण ज़िक्र दिखा देता है कि सरहद का सदमा भाषा की पाठशाला तक घुस आया था।

panels.shot: montage-style wide with faint superimposed scenes: court debates, frontier scouts, merchants
panels.action: A blended scene shows a Magadhan council debating, scouts watching a dusty track in the northwest, and merchants weighing coins, all sharing the same muted color tone.

dialogue.text: We can imagine, but cannot assert: councils in Pataliputra debating the threat, frontier chiefs watching the roads, trade routes shifting as Yavana and Indian authorities tested each other’s reach.

i18n.hi: हम केवल कल्पना कर सकते हैं, दावा नहीं: पाटलिपुत्र की सभाएँ खतरे पर बहस करतीं, सीमा के सरदार रास्ते नापते, और व्यापार-पथ बदलते जब यवन और भारतीय अफ़सर एक-दूसरे की पहुंच टटोलते।

panels.shot: tense interior of a Magadhan council with Pushyamitra at its center
panels.action: Pushyamitra Shunga sits in a wooden hall lit by torches, councillors around him; his face is drawn but firm, a map of the middle Ganga laid before him, northwest routes marked with pebbles.

dialogue.speaker: pushyamitra_shunga_and_menander_i
dialogue.text: We rule no longer in Ashoka’s shadow, but under new clouds; we must learn this sky.

i18n.hi: हम अब अशोक की छाया में नहीं, नई घटाओं के नीचे राज करते हैं; हमें इस नए आसमान को पढ़ना सीखना होगा।

panels.shot: mid-shot of Menander in a tent at night, studying a map adorned with city names
panels.action: By lamplight in a canvas tent, Menander I leans over a map where Greek and Prakrit names mingle, his finger hovering near the central plain, his face thoughtful and unresolved.

dialogue.text: Did Menander himself ever stand before Saketa or dream of Pataliputra? The coins and the texts speak, but they do not answer with certainty; historians argue the line his campaigns truly traced.

i18n.hi: क्या खुद मेनान्दर कभी साकेत के सामने खड़ा हुआ, या पाटलिपुत्र का सपना देखता रहा? सिक्के और ग्रंथ बोलते हैं, पर साफ़ जवाब नहीं देते; इतिहासकार अब भी उसके असली अभियान की लकीर पर भिड़े हैं।

panels.shot: illustrated page of the Yuga Purana being read aloud by a later reciter
panels.action: Centuries later, a reciter in simple robes holds a manuscript of the Yuga Purana, gesturing as he narrates imagined Yavana advances, listeners gathered in a dim hall, rapt.

dialogue.text: Later, the Yuga Purana would speak in a prophetic voice of Yavanas pressing toward even Pataliputra, blending memory and imagination into a warning about how ages crumble and new powers test old walls.

i18n.hi: बाद में युगपुराण भविष्यवाणी की आवाज़ में यवनों के पाटलिपुत्र तक दबाव की बात करेगा, याद और कल्पना मिलाकर यह चेतावनी बनेगी कि युग कैसे ढहते हैं और नई ताकतें पुरानी दीवारों को आज़माती हैं।

panels.shot: close-up of a modern historian’s hand comparing a coin, the Mahabhashya manuscript, and Yuga Purana pages
panels.action: On a modern wooden desk, a hand places an Indo-Greek coin beside a copy of the Mahabhashya and a Yuga Purana folio, the three artefacts forming a triangle of evidence.

dialogue.text: Today we lace together Patanjali’s offhand example, the schematic Yuga Purana and the cold shine of coins to see the outline of a time when Indo-Greek and Shunga horizons overlapped uneasily.

i18n.hi: आज हम पतंजलि का यूँ ही दिया उदाहरण, युगपुराण की खाका-सी कथा और सिक्कों की ठंडी चमक जोड़कर उस दौर की रूपरेखा देखते हैं, जब यवन-यूनानी और शुंग सीमाएँ असहज होकर टकराती थीं।

panels.shot: wide closing shot of a quiet classroom again, the landscape beyond visible through an open doorway
panels.action: Back in an ancient-style classroom, a teacher and students sit over palm leaves, the open doorway framing fields and a distant road, peaceful under a soft sky.

dialogue.text: A single, calm line in a grammar book has carried to us the tremor of that age, when Magadha learned that the northwest frontier had changed, and even the rules of language had to watch a war pass by.

i18n.hi: एक सीधी, शांत पंक्ति ने व्याकरण की किताब से उस युग की थरथराहट हमें पहुँचा दी, जब मगध ने जाना कि उत्तर-पश्चिम की सरहद बदल चुकी है, और भाषा के नियमों तक को गुजरती जंग को देखना पड़ा।

title_i18n.en: The Grammar That Watched a War

subtitle_i18n.en: When a Sanskrit Line Heard the Yavanas March
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब संस्कृत पंक्ति ने यवनों की चाल सुनी
